faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella in April for a boat trip?
faq.a: April in Marbella averages 22°C highs and 12°C lows, with sea temperatures around 16°C. Sunshine hours increase to about 8 per day, and rain is infrequent (typically 4–5 days in the month). Light winds from the east or west keep the sea manageable, though mornings can be cooler — a light jacket is advisable.

faq.q: Is Easter 2035 early or late in April?
faq.a: Easter Sunday 2035 falls on 1 April, making it one of the earliest possible dates. This means the Easter holidays will be in the first week of April. Bookings tend to spike from mid-March, so we recommend reserving your boat 4–6 weeks in advance to secure your preferred model and time slot.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a group of 10 in April?
faq.a: For 10 passengers, the Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Astondoa 40 (9 pax) are solid choices from our Tier A fleet, both at €749/2h. If you want more space, the Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) or Pershing 46 (10 pax) offer extra comfort. All depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper, drinks, and snacks.

faq.q: Can I rent a smaller boat for just my family?
faq.a: Yes. For up to 5 passengers, the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) are ideal, and the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) works well for a smaller group. These are priced on request via WhatsApp. All include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and VAT — no hidden extras.

faq.q: What should I wear for a boat trip in Marbella in April?
faq.a: Layers are key. A light jumper or jacket for the morning departure (around 10:00), then shorts or a dress by midday when it warms to 22°C. Bring sunscreen (SPF 30+), sunglasses, and a windbreaker. The sea breeze can feel cool at 20 knots, so a zip-up is useful even in sunshine.

faq.q: How far can we sail from Puerto Banús in a 4-hour charter?
faq.a: In 4 hours you can easily reach Cala del Faro (15 NM west) or Cabopino (8 NM east), with time for a swim stop. The Mangusta 80 (24m) can cover more distance at 28 knots, but most charters stay within 10–20 NM of the marina to maximise relaxation time.

faq.q: Are there any Easter events on the coast we can see from the boat?
faq.a: Marbella's Easter processions (Semana Santa) are mostly inland, but you can watch from the sea as processions pass near the Paseo Marítimo. Puerto Banús itself hosts a small Easter market. For a quieter day, head to Cala Cortés or Estepona — both offer calm anchorages with coastal views.

faq.q: Do I need to book a skipper or can I drive myself?
faq.a: All our charters include a licensed skipper as standard. Spanish regulations require a professional captain for rental boats over 6m unless you hold a valid Spanish or ICC licence. Our skippers know the local waters, anchor spots, and weather patterns, so you can relax completely.

data.body_html:
Easter 2035 lands on 1 April, making it one of the earliest Easters in recent years. If you're planning a Marbella boat rental weather April 2035 Easter trip, you'll want to know what conditions to expect and how to book smartly. This guide covers average temperatures, sea states, boat recommendations, and practical tips for a smooth charter from Puerto Banús.

Whether you're celebrating with family or friends, our fleet of 16+ yachts offers options for every group size and budget. All depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT — no surprise costs.

April Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

April in Marbella brings mild, pleasant spring weather. Average daily highs reach 22°C (72°F), while overnight lows dip to around 12°C (54°F). Sea temperatures hover near 16°C, so swimming is possible but bracing — a wetsuit isn't necessary, but a quick dip is refreshing rather than tropical.

  • Sunshine: 8 hours per day on average
  • Rainfall: 35 mm over 4–5 days
  • Wind: Light to moderate, 10–15 knots from east or west
  • Sea state: Calm to slight (1–2 on the Douglas scale)

Morning departures (10:00–12:00) can be cool — bring a light jacket or fleece. By midday, the sun warms the deck nicely. Afternoon sea breezes pick up around 15:00, so a windbreaker is handy for the return leg.

Best Boats for Your Easter 2035 Charter

Our fleet ranges from compact speedboats to superyachts. For a group of 9–11, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (Tier A) are excellent value at €749 for 2 hours (including skipper, drinks, and VAT). For a premium experience, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski.

Smaller groups (5–6 pax) can choose the Dubhe (8m), Mariah SX21 (6.4m), or Speedboat (7m) — all priced on request via WhatsApp. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, soft drinks, beer, wine, cava, and light snacks.

Easter 2035 Dates & Booking Window

Easter Sunday 2035 falls on 1 April. Holy Week (Semana Santa) runs from Palm Sunday (25 March) to Easter Monday (2 April). Demand for boat rentals peaks during this period, especially in Puerto Banús. We recommend booking 4–6 weeks in advance to secure your preferred boat and time slot.

Most charters operate between 10:00 and 20:00. Half-day (4h) and full-day (8h) options are available. For the best light and calmest sea, aim for a 10:00–14:00 or 11:00–15:00 slot. Sunset cruises (18:00–20:00) are also popular in April as the days lengthen.

Where to Go: Top Destinations from Puerto Banús

Within a 4-hour charter, you can reach several scenic spots:

  • Cala del Faro (15 NM west) — a quiet cove with clear water, ideal for anchoring
  • Cabopino (8 NM east) — a sandy beach with a protected dune system
  • Estepona (12 NM west) — a charming fishing port with waterfront restaurants
  • Marbella Marina (5 NM east) — the historic harbour with views of La Concha mountain

For a full-day trip, you can push to Sotogrande (25 NM west) or explore the Golden Mile coastline. Your skipper will tailor the route to your preferences and the day's weather.

What's Included in Every Charter

All our rentals include:

  • Licensed English-speaking skipper
  • Fuel for the trip
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (chips, olives, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21% VAT)

No hidden extras. You can bring your own food or arrange catering — just let us know when you book. For the Mangusta 80, the free jet ski adds extra fun for watersports.

Tips for a Smooth Easter Charter

  1. Dress in layers — a fleece or hoodie for morning, then shorts by midday.
  2. Bring sunscreen — UV is moderate but reflection off the water intensifies it.
  3. Arrive 15 minutes early at Puerto Banús to meet your skipper and board.
  4. Communicate dietary needs — we can adjust snacks and drinks.
  5. Check the forecast — April can have occasional showers; your skipper will advise.
